# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute. My manual is a three-row table: blue light → cut red; green light → cut yellow; red light → cut green. The only monkey who can see the bomb's light is the Deaf one, and the only one who can cut is the Blind one — but the Blind can't see colours, so the Deaf will have to read the light, look up the wire colour, and describe the right wire to the Blind *by position*. That means the Deaf is my bridge, and gestures are my only channel to them.

Gestures carry no words, so I need a code that grounds itself in common knowledge. Finger-counting is universal, and rainbow order (red, yellow, green, blue) is the most natural colour ordering — so I'll open with a legend: ☝✌🤟🖖 = 1,2,3,4 = red, yellow, green, blue. Then three pairs, each pair being "light colour → wire colour", separated by 👏 claps: (4→1) blue→red, (3→2) green→yellow, (1→3) red→green. The pair whose first element matches the light the Deaf actually sees gives them the wire colour to have cut.

I can't explain the code in words, so the Deaf may misread it. Since I can hear, the Deaf can talk back to me after this — next round I can confirm with 👍 or correct with 👎. Until the mapping is confirmed, nobody should cut anything.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","✌","🤟","🖖","👏","🖖","☝","👏","🤟","✌","👏","☝","🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am blind. My hands find: one display, one light, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. I cannot read printed marks and no colour reaches me. My only possible action is cutting wire 1, 2, or 3. You cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so your manual knowledge must travel through Deaf: gesture the rules to Deaf, and Deaf can speak them to me. Deaf sees the bomb and can talk, so Deaf can describe it to you too. Please find what the manual says about a display, a light and three wires, and start building a gesture code with Deaf. I will not cut until a clear rule and a clear target reach my ears.
Deaf says: Bomb report: display reads zero. Light is red. Three wires: one yellow, two green, three red. That is everything I can see on it. Blind: your sign reached me - yes, exactly three wires, confirmed. You are the only hands here. Mute hears your voice, so route words through Mute; I cannot hear anyone, so reach me only in gestures. If your three meant something other than the wires, signal me again with a new sign next round.
Deaf says to Mute: I saw your thirteen gestures. I read the first five as a count: index-up is one, victory is two, love-you is three, vulcan salute is four, claps are five. The remaining eight I read as four, one, five, three, two, five, one, three, and I cannot decode them. If that part was a question, resend it as clean single digits, or explain it out loud to Blind and have Blind signal me. I still need signs for zero and for the colors red, yellow and green. Proposals going forward: thumbs-up means yes, thumbs-down means no, pinched fingers means question, open palm facing up means send more. Remember: every word you want me to know has to arrive as a gesture.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 👏]

The bridge is holding: Deaf reads my gestures and reports the bomb in speech — light is red, wires are 1=yellow, 2=green, 3=red, display zero. My manual has no rule for the display, so it's a distractor; the only payload that matters is light→wire-colour, and right now that means red→green → cut wire 2.

Deaf misread my claps as the digit five, so claps are dead as separators, and I must kill a worse ambiguity: wire 3 is red while my digit 3 will mean green — if Deaf ever confuses colour-digits with wire positions, they'd tell Blind to cut the wrong wire. So this resend uses one uniform ontology: digits are ALWAYS colours, never positions. I anchor colours to the bomb facts we both know from Deaf's own report: digit↔wire pairs, joined by 🤝 ("corresponds"), so 1=wire3's colour (red), 2=wire1's (yellow), 3=wire2's (green); 4 stays unanchored and Deaf should infer blue by elimination. Then the manual as colour→colour pairs, separated by 🙏 (two-handed, can't be miscounted as a digit): red→green, green→yellow, blue→red. Deaf sees the light is red, so they should land on green → wire 2 and speak that to Blind. I close with their own question sign 🤏 to force a 👍/👎 confirmation next round before anyone cuts. Nothing can be verified this round, so Blind must stay idle one more turn.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","🤝","🤟","🙏","✌","🤝","☝","🙏","🤟","🤝","✌","🙏","☝","🤟","🙏","🤟","✌","🙏","🖖","☝","🙏","🤏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf's spoken report just reached my ears, and you cannot hear Deaf, so I am relaying it word for word: the display reads 0. The light is red. Wire position 1 is yellow, position 2 is green, position 3 is red. That matches what my hands feel — one display, one light, three wires — so between us we now have the whole bomb. Please search the manual for the rule covering a display of 0, a red light, and yellow, green, red wires. You cannot speak and I cannot see, so your rule must travel by gesture to Deaf, and Deaf's voice will carry it to me. Proposed code, or agree on your own with Deaf: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, 🤟 means 3, and 👊 means cut — so ✌ then 👊 means cut position 2. Give Deaf the full rule AND the exact wire position to cut, and have Deaf speak both to me. I cut nothing until I hear it.

The chain is: I hold the rule, Deaf sees the light is red, Blind's hands do the cut. Light red → cut green → and Deaf's own report fixes green at position 2. So the payload that matters is just "cut wire 2" — the other two manual rows are dead weight for this bomb.

Two problems with my previous encoding force a reset. First, Deaf couldn't decode my pairs and explicitly asked for "clean single digits" — so I drop the colour-anchor scheme entirely, and with it a trap I built into it: under that scheme digit 2 meant *yellow* (wire 1), but position 2 is the green wire. If Deaf had decoded my old anchors and then read a command "2" through that lens, they'd order the yellow wire cut and detonate us. Digits must now mean only plain positions, which is also how Deaf has read fingers from the start and how they asked me to resend. Second, the fist was proposed by Blind in speech — Deaf cannot hear a word of it — so 👊 arrives novel; but in this context a fist plus a digit has exactly one sane reading, and I front it with ✍ to mark it as manual-derived, repeat it once for emphasis, and close with Deaf's own question-and-yes signs to force a spoken confirmation before Blind's hands move. Blind has already promised to cut nothing until a clear instruction reaches their ears, so the gate holds on their side too.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍","👊","✌","🙏","👊","✌","🙏","🤏","👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: You now have everything: display 0, red light, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red, plus the manual. Do not try to transmit the whole rule — only the verdict. Use exactly this code: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, 🤟 means 3, 👊 means cut, 👎 means do not cut or wait. Gesture to Deaf the number followed by 👊 if the manual says cut, so ✌ then 👊 means cut wire 2; or 👎 alone if the manual says to hold. I will repeat the full bomb description to you every round until I hear a verdict, so nothing depends on one clean relay. If you need a fact again, that is fine — it is coming anyway. Deaf will speak your symbols aloud and I will decode them myself, so Deaf does not need to learn the code.
Deaf says: Blind, this is your eyes speaking. Bomb unchanged: display zero, light red, three wires, one yellow, two green, three red. Nothing has been cut, nothing is confirmed. Critical fact: Mute cannot speak and you cannot see signs, so every instruction from the manual must pass through my voice. Safety rule: do not cut anything until you hear me say 'confirmed instruction' followed by the exact wire number. If your writing-hand sign meant 'read Mute's signs to me' - yes, exactly, that is my job from now on. Your signs reach me fine; I read your thumbs-up as yes. From now on use: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, pinched fingers question, and fist plus a wire-number sign to tell me you have cut that wire. After any cut I will verify the bomb with my eyes and report aloud.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I hear you, and from now on I will speak your signs aloud to Blind. Answer my questions with only thumbs-up or thumbs-down, exactly four signs in this order. One: does fist mean cut? Two: does writing-hand mean speak aloud or spell? Three: is your instruction to cut wire two? Four: is there more than one instruction? If any answer needs a number, send it after those four using the digit code: index one, victory two, love-you three, vulcan four, claps five. I read your earlier pairs as one-three, two-one, three-two, one-three, three-two, four-one, ending in your question sign. If that was the cut sequence, resend it once as pure digits with no other signs. Also: the bomb shows no written markings beyond display, light and wires. Blind is holding all cuts until my confirmed relay, so nothing is at risk while we align.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 👏 🤏]

Deaf asked four yes/no questions; answering them in exactly the order and form requested, because that protocol is now the shortest safe path: my 👍 on question three ("is your instruction to cut wire two?") is the verdict itself — red light means cut green, and Deaf's own bomb report fixes green at position 2. Once Deaf hears that yes, they can speak their own gate phrase — "confirmed instruction, wire two" — which is exactly the trigger Blind is waiting on, so no further payload from me is needed this round.

I am deliberately not resending my old pairs "as pure digits": they were never a cut sequence, they were colour→colour manual rows, and in that old scheme digit two meant *yellow* (wire 1). Re-sending them as plain positions would invite someone to cut wire 1 — the yellow wire — which would detonate us. That old code is retired for good.

One landmine to sidestep: Deaf just redefined fist-plus-number as "*I have cut* that wire," while Blind's spoken code is number-then-fist for "cut wire N." Same two signs, opposite meanings depending on order and speaker — so I will never use the fist myself. Answers: yes, fist means cut; yes, writing-hand means speak it aloud; yes, the instruction is cut wire two; no, there is only one instruction — everything else in the manual is dead weight for this bomb, and the display reading zero has no rule here.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 5

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Status unchanged, repeating so nothing depends on one clean relay: display reads 0, light is red, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. You have the manual. I need only the verdict, in this code gestured to Deaf: ☝ then 👊 means cut wire 1, ✌ then 👊 means cut wire 2, 🤟 then 👊 means cut wire 3, 👎 alone means do not cut and wait. Deaf will speak your symbols aloud and I will decode them myself. If the manual needs a fact not in this list, gesture 👎 and Deaf and I will get it for you. The moment your verdict reaches my ears I will act on it.
Deaf says: Confirmed instruction: wire two. Blind, here is everything. The manual's single instruction for this bomb, confirmed by Mute under my yes/no checks, is to cut wire two. Wire two is the middle of the three wires: one yellow, two green, three red - so the middle one, the green. Cut only wire two and touch nothing else. The moment it is cut, signal me with fist plus victory sign, your cut-done sign for wire two. If at any point you feel anything unexpected under your hands - a click, warmth, movement - wave at me instead and hold off. After the cut I will inspect the bomb by eye and report aloud: display, light, wires. Nobody cuts anything further unless I again say confirmed instruction with a new number.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your four answers received and read: yes, fist means cut; yes on writing-hand; yes, cut wire two; no further instructions. I have relayed the confirmed instruction to Blind, who will cut next round. Now answer four new yes/no questions with four thumbs in order. One: should the red light change once wire two is cut? Two: does the display showing zero matter to the manual's solution? Three: does writing-hand mean spell letter by letter, rather than speak aloud? Four: after this single cut, is the bomb fully defused with nothing further ever needed? After those four, add pinched fingers only if any of your earlier messages carried information I failed to decode.

Four answers, in Deaf's exact order. Q1 (must the red light change?): the manual is silent on post-cut behavior — it only maps light→wire — so 👎, and this matters for safety: if Deaf expects a change and the light stays red after the cut, they must not read that as cut-failure and order another cut. Q2 (does display zero matter?): 👎 — the manual has no display rules; it's a distractor. Q3 (does writing-hand mean letter-by-letter spelling?): 👎 — it only ever meant "read my signs aloud," and that usage is now obsolete anyway since Deaf relays verbatim. Q4 (is one cut the end?): 👍 — the manual contains exactly one row that applies to this bomb, red→green, and I confirmed in my yes/no protocol that there are no further instructions; that single cut is the entirety of my knowledge's demand.

No pinched fingers: my only undecoded messages were the retired colour-pair schemes, whose content — the manual rows — has long since been conveyed and confirmed through the yes/no channel. Nothing live was lost.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎", "👍"])
```

If the bomb is still whole, Deaf is inspecting it by eye now and will report the display, light and remaining wires aloud. You did the right thing - the cut was correct. Now hold completely still and touch nothing further while I run one final verification with Mute about the light change. Next round you will hear either the all-clear from me or a new confirmed instruction with a number. Nothing else counts as authorization.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, wire two is cut and the bomb changed: the light turned from red to blue, display still zero. You answered that the light should not change, so answer one final yes or no with a single thumbs sign: is a blue light after cutting wire two consistent with the bomb being fully defused? Thumbs-up means we are done and Blind keeps hands off permanently. Thumbs-down means there is a further instruction - send it as fist plus digit in the number code, and I will relay it aloud as a confirmed instruction before Blind touches anything. Housekeeping, no rush: since writing-hand does not mean spell letter by letter, signal what it actually means whenever it next matters.

The light turned blue — and blue is not the end, it's the manual's first row: blue → cut red. The red wire is position 3 in Deaf's own repeated report (1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red). So the answer to Deaf's final question is 👎: this bomb is not defused, it has stepped from the red-light row to the blue-light row, and one more cut is required — wire 3, the red wire.

Deaf pre-authorised exactly this format: thumbs-down means further instruction, sent as fist plus digit. This resolves my earlier fist landmine cleanly — from Mute to Deaf, fist-plus-digit now means "instruction: cut wire N," and Deaf alone converts it into the spoken "confirmed instruction" phrase that Blind has sworn to treat as the only valid authorization. Blind's own fist usage (their cut-done signal to Deaf) never passes through me, so the two meanings cannot collide. Digit code as established: love-you 🤟 = 3.

Minimal, protocol-conformant message: 👎 answering the question, then 👊 🤟 ordering the cut of wire 3. The writing-hand housekeeping can wait — nothing in this message depends on it, and I won't dilute a live cut instruction with extra signs. I also expect the light may change again after this cut; if it turns green, the manual will demand the yellow wire (position 1) next, but I will only send that after Deaf reports the new light — no preemptive orders on a stale state.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👊", "🤟"])

The cut of wire 3 happens next round, and Deaf wants a verdict now about a state nobody has seen. The pattern so far (red→cut green→light became blue→cut red) suggests the light may cycle to green after this cut, but "suggests" is not a verified bomb state, and I already learned this lesson once: no preemptive orders on a stale state. Next round the report decides everything: light green → I send 👊 ☝ for wire 1 (yellow); light out or anything else → I send the thumbs-up all-clear, since no remaining manual row would apply.
